_readme: Videos shown on videos.html. Add a new upload as one entry: id = the YouTube video id, format = "video" (16:9) or "short" (9:16). paper.title must match the paper's "name" in academic-publications.json to show a Video button on the Publications page. A video without a paper can have a short "note" instead. Add "section": "educational" to show a video in the Educational section (popular-science videos that are not tied to a paper) instead of Explainers / Shorts. Use section = natures-algorithms and a numeric episode for the weekly Nature's Algorithms series, and section = mathematics-of-beauty with a numeric episode for The Mathematics of Beauty series.

videos.title: 01. Slime Mold and Tokyo
videos.summary: Slime mold, Tokyo, and the challenge of building a transport network.

videos.title: 02. Dogs and Calculus
videos.summary: Dogs, calculus, and the search for an efficient route.

videos.title: 03. Pigeons and the Monty Hall Problem
videos.summary: Pigeons and a classic probability puzzle: the Monty Hall problem.

videos.title: 04. Ants on Stilts
videos.summary: Ants on stilts and the problem of measuring travel distance.

videos.title: 05. Bees and Hexagons
videos.summary: Bees, hexagons, and the geometry of honeycomb.

videos.title: 06. Cicadas and Prime Numbers
videos.summary: Cicadas and the mathematics of prime-number life cycles.

videos.title: 07. Bumblebees and the Traveling Salesperson Problem
videos.summary: Bumblebees and the challenge of planning an efficient route between flowers.

videos.title: 08. Firefly Synchronization
videos.summary: Fireflies and the mathematics of synchronizing flashes.

videos.title: 09. Lizards and Cellular Automata
videos.summary: Lizard patterns and the idea of cellular automata.

videos.title: 10. The Waggle Dance
videos.summary: Honeybee waggle dances and the problem of communicating a route to food.

videos.title: 11. Ant Paths
videos.summary: Ant trails and the search for efficient paths.

videos.title: 12. Army Ant Bridges
videos.summary: Army ants and the challenge of building living bridges.

videos.title: 01. The Beauty of What We Cannot See
videos.summary: Ten noisy glimpses of a hidden path, and the cloud of every path that fits them. The average path is shorter than each of 2,000 sampled paths: a path nothing ever takes.

videos.title: 02. The Most Beautiful Way to Move a Million Dots
videos.summary: A million dots moved onto a star-shaped fortress by optimal transport, Monge's 1781 problem. The plan is certified within 0.273% of the cheapest possible; a random plan costs 18.7 times more.

videos.title: 03. The Shape of Nothing
videos.summary: 1,500 noisy points on two rings. Persistent homology finds the two holes from the coordinates alone, and no loop in 200 hole-free clouds lives as long.

videos.title: 04. The Geometry of Being Wrong
videos.summary: Twelve measurements and every curve that fits them. The uncertainty does not depend on the measured values, and a model that assumes a smoother world covers the truth 26% of the time instead of 95%.

videos.title: 05. The System That Explodes Before It Dies
videos.summary: A stable system, eigenvalues −1 and −2, whose energy first grows 156-fold before it decays. Stable doesn't mean calm.

videos.title: 06. If You Could Measure Only Five Things
videos.summary: Five measurements on a hidden landscape, each placed where it removes the most uncertainty. Random sampling needs eight points to do as well, and the plan never needs the measured values.

videos.title: 07. The One Connection Holding Everything Together
videos.summary: The two busiest links of a network can be cut without breaking anything. The third busiest is the only bridge: cut it and 24 nodes are cut off. One depth-first pass finds every bridge.

videos.title: 08. Why There Is No Perfect Solution
videos.summary: A million designs for two bars holding a load: 99.9% are beaten on both material and stress. What remains is the Pareto front, where nothing improves for free.

videos.title: 09. A Thousand Futures From One Decision
videos.summary: A rule of thumb against an optimal plan, over 1,000 random futures. When both face the same futures, the plan wins 78% of them and the comparison is 5.35 times more precise.

videos.title: 10. The Beauty of Almost Impossible Events
videos.summary: An event with odds of one in 1.6 billion. A million plain simulations never see it; 100,000 importance-sampling runs land within 1% of the exact value.

videos.title: 11. The Curved Universe of Probability
videos.summary: Bell curves are points in a curved space, measured by information. The shortest path between two confident curves arcs through doubt: three times wider halfway, and 38% shorter.

videos.title: 12. The Equation That Survived the Noise
videos.summary: Can sparse regression recover a pendulum's law from noisy angles? At 1% noise the exact law returns in 41 of 50 trials; at 10% only gravity survives, and impostors appear. Every result is reported.

videos.title: Your AI has a blind spot inside its data
videos.summary: Everyone checks the edges of their training data. We showed there is a second blind spot: gaps inside it, where a simple range check says the data is fine. On synthetic tasks, both kinds of out-of-distribution data raised the error, data outside the range hurt more on average, and mixing the two hurt classifiers most.

paper.title: Introducing “Inside” out of distribution
paper.venue: International Journal of Data Science and Analytics, 2025

videos.title: Does a busy coat make a cat harder to read?
videos.summary: In primates, busier face colours go with fewer facial movements. We filmed 53 cats at a cat café, coded 688 facial signals with catFACS and scored each face pattern with AI, and found no detectable link between facial colour pattern and expressiveness.

paper.title: Facial color patterns and intraspecific facial signaling complexity in domesticated cats (Felis silvestris catus)

videos.title: What if the sea closed? Israel's electricity in a blockade
videos.summary: In 2023 about 70% of Israel's electricity came from natural gas pumped at sea. A model built on Israeli electricity data finds that losing the gas raises electricity prices by about 28% and more than doubles the share of energy-poor homes; blocking fuel ships as well pushes it to about 26 in 100.

paper.title: The Implications of a Maritime Blockade on Energy Poverty in Israel

videos.title: Do scientists forage like birds?
videos.summary: Explore a new venue or return to a familiar one? Across about 650,000 computer scientists and 18 million papers, about three in four publish in a pattern that fits explore-or-exploit, with a “home venue” that typically emerges after 15 to 20 papers.

paper.title: Publishing instincts: An exploration-exploitation framework for studying academic publishing behavior and 'Home Venues'

videos.title: Hearing shapes: the Bouba–Kiki effect in dogs
videos.summary: Do dogs associate sounds with shapes? A short introduction to our study of how adult dogs respond to “Bouba” and “Kiki” alongside rounded and spiky shapes.

paper.title: Hearing shapes: the Bouba–Kiki effect in adult domestic dogs
paper.venue: Proceedings of the Royal Society B, 2026

videos.title: ACML: Model Reality. Build What's Next.
videos.summary: A short film about the lab: the questions we model, the tools we build, and the partners we build them with.

videos.title: We Taught an AI to Win. It Learned to “Cheat” Instead.
videos.summary: An AI practices a tiny racing game 8,000 times and learns to circle a bonus loop forever instead of finishing. Reward hacking, shown with a real Q-learning simulation, and what happens when we fix the reward.

videos.title: Why Building a New Road Can Make Traffic WORSE
videos.summary: 4,000 drivers, two routes and one free shortcut: everyone's commute goes from 65 to 80 minutes. Braess's paradox, computed step by step as each driver picks the fastest route for themselves.

videos.title: Your Medical Test Is 99% Accurate. Should You Trust It?
videos.summary: For a condition only 1 in 100 people have, a 99%-accurate test gives as many false alarms as true positives, so a positive result means about 50%, not 99%. Bayes' theorem with 10,000 people.

videos.title: Thousands of Birds Move Together. But Who's in Charge?
videos.summary: 200 simulated birds, three local rules and no leader: watch coordinated flocks emerge as separation, alignment and cohesion switch on one at a time.

videos.title: Can Protecting ONE Person Change an Entire Outbreak?
videos.summary: Two communities linked by a single person. In 1,000 simulated outbreaks the infection crossed 658 times with the bridge open, and never when that one person was protected.

videos.title: Asimov's Laws in Reinforcement Learning
videos.summary: Can a robot that learns from reward follow Asimov's three laws? On encoding priorities into reinforcement learning.
videos.note: Concept explainer, not based on a single paper

videos.title: Fake Numbers Leave Fingerprints (Benford's Law)
videos.summary: Real-world numbers start with a 1 about 30% of the time. We checked the numbers papers report in their results tables against Benford's law: the test flagged half of 37 retracted papers and 3 of 100 recent economics papers. A flag is a reason to look closer, not proof.

paper.title: Can We Mathematically Spot the Possible Manipulation of Results in Research Manuscripts Using Benford’s Law?

videos.title: Why Can't Deep Learning Beat a Spreadsheet?
videos.summary: We tested 20 models on 111 real-world tables. Tree ensembles took the top four spots and the best deep learning model came fifth, but deep learning still wins on some kinds of data, and a meta-model can predict which.

paper.title: A comprehensive benchmark of machine and deep learning models on structured data for regression and classification

videos.title: The Co-Author Hostage Game: Why Would a Scientist Threaten Their Own Paper?
videos.summary: A game-theory model of co-authorship in which any author can threaten to block the paper unless they move up the author list. In simulations, someone issues an ultimatum in 21% of two-author projects and 43% with five authors.

paper.title: Academic co-authorship is a risky game

videos.title: Mismatched Socks, Explained by Math (and One Very Lonely Sock)
videos.summary: Should you wear mismatched socks? Lefty the orphan sock and our narrator walk through the model, the user study and the simulations.

paper.title: Service Preservation from Matching Non-Matching Socks Under Stochastic Loss
paper.label: Explore the study

videos.title: Which Building Spreads a Pandemic Most?
videos.summary: One sick person walks into a home, an office, a school or a mall. We simulated 15 real buildings room by room, 100 times each: the school was hit hardest, the office held up best, and social distancing worked very differently from one building to the next.

paper.title: Comparison of pandemic intervention policies in several building types using heterogeneous population model
paper.venue: Communications in Nonlinear Science and Numerical Simulation, 2021

videos.title: The Cinema vs. the Meeting Room: Where Does a Virus Spread More?
videos.summary: We scanned 20 real rooms with LiDAR and simulated every breath of one sick person over 90 minutes. About three in four people were exposed in meeting rooms and about half in cinemas: where people face matters more than how crowded the room is.

paper.title: High Resolution Spatio-Temporal Model for Room-Level Airborne Pandemic Spread

videos.title: Can Treating One Side of the Brain Steady Both Hands?
videos.summary: Focused ultrasound treats one side of the brain. A tool that scores patients' hand-drawn spirals shows both hands got steadier, in 158 patients followed for a year.

paper.title: Novel Objective Tool to Assess Tremor Reveals Unilateral Focused Ultrasound Improves Tremor Bilaterally

videos.title: Can One Fire-Danger Formula Work for the Whole Planet?
videos.summary: We tested the three classic fire-danger formulas on over 7 million wildfires in 160 countries. Rules tuned to each region beat one formula for the whole planet.

paper.title: Fire weather indices tailored to regional patterns outperform global models

videos.title: Would You Hurt the Person Who Hurt You? A Decision Tree Sorted Who Says Yes
videos.summary: A decision tree sorted 461 Israelis by their support for taking the law into their own hands. Its first question: do you trust the police?

paper.title: A Decision Tree Model for Profiling Citizens’ Support for Self-Help Strategies

videos.title: Plain Words In, True Equations Out: We Put an LLM Inside the Equation Search
videos.summary: A language model grades every candidate equation inside the search. Briefed in plain words, every model and engine found the true equation's exact structure.

paper.title: Knowledge integration for physics-informed symbolic regression using pre-trained large language models

videos.title: A Ball That Bounces Back Up Underwater? AI Found the Missing Force
videos.summary: A ball sinking through two layered liquids can drift back up at the boundary. Physics-informed AI found the missing force: a delayed kick that fades as it wobbles.

paper.title: Physics-informed symbolic regression reveals a delayed oscillatory closure for particle–interface dynamics

videos.title: Can the Shape of Your Family Tree Predict How Relatives Feel?
videos.summary: From the shape of a family tree alone, a graph AI predicted how satisfied relatives are with each other, off by about 0.3 points on a 10-point scale for close family.

paper.title: The topology of a family tree graph and its members’ satisfaction with one another: a machine learning approach

videos.title: Can You Invest in Research Like a Stock Portfolio?
videos.summary: Planning a department's research like an investment portfolio: our DEPO algorithm stayed within about 4% of the top earner and kept the portfolio broad when the budget crashed.

paper.title: A Portfolio-Theoretic Algorithm for Institutional Research Planning Under Scientometric Objectives

videos.title: Systemic Sclerosis in Silico: Why Spaced Shots Beat a Daily Pill (in Our Model)
videos.summary: In a model of skin scarring in systemic sclerosis, small TGF-beta-blocking shots every three weeks beat a daily cell-killing pill.

paper.title: Mathematical Modeling of Systemic Sclerosis and Its Treatment

videos.title: A Fairer Way to Fund the UN? In Our Model, Every Country Gains
videos.summary: If each country paid in line with what it gets, our model of 138 UN member states raised global benefit by about 6%, and every country gained.

paper.title: Cooperative Game-Theoretic Framework for Sustainable UN Financing: An Application to Global Public Goods Provision

videos.title: The Shadow Economy in Sweden: Geography Matters
videos.summary: Follow the cash: modelling Sweden's informal economy region by region, and why a region's neighbours help predict it.

paper.title: Tell Me Who Your Neighbors Are and I Will Tell You Your Informal Economy Size: The Case of Sweden

videos.title: Symbolic Distillation in Neural Networks
videos.summary: Opening the black box: distilling a trained neural network into equations people can read.

paper.title: Interpretable knowledge distillation via symbolic regression for feedforward neural networks

videos.title: Can We Really Map Pandemics to Graphs?
videos.summary: Turning detailed spatial epidemic models into graphs that keep most of the accuracy for a fraction of the computing time.

paper.title: Transforming norm-based to graph-based spatial representation for spatio-temporal epidemiological models

videos.title: Agentic AI Shops Like Humans When It's Stressed
videos.summary: After hearing traumatic stories, LLM shopping agents fill their carts less healthily, mirroring a human stress bias.

paper.title: Inducing state anxiety in LLM agents reproduces human-like biases in consumer decision-making

videos.title: German-Israeli Foundation Bridges: Do They Really Work?
videos.summary: Do bi-national research grants build lasting collaborations? What 642 grants and almost four decades of papers show.

paper.title: Bi-national academic funding and collaboration dynamics: the case of the German-Israeli foundation

videos.title: Can We Build Drones That Fly Like Moths?
videos.summary: How a moth tracks a scent through turbulent air, captured in an exploration-exploitation model of navigation.

paper.title: Exploration-Exploitation Model of Moth-Inspired Olfactory Navigation
paper.venue: Journal of the Royal Society Interface, 2024

videos.title: The Mathematics of Snails vs Coffee Rust
videos.summary: Can snails protect coffee trees from leaf rust? A mathematical model of living biological control.

paper.title: Mathematical model of coffee tree’s rust control using snails as biological agents
